name: Dialog
description: A modal dialog on the platform's own `<dialog>`: `showModal()` supplies the top layer, the `::backdrop`, an inert page behind it, Escape, focus containment and focus return — so none of that is written here.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens it, handed the ref and props that wire it up. Leave it out to open the dialog from anywhere else.

props.name: children
props.description: The dialog's content — a `Dialog.Title`, usually a `Dialog.Description`, and the controls.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Leave it out and the dialog owns it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open, when the dialog owns its own state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires with the new state and why it changed — `'trigger'`, `'escape'`, `'outside-pointer'` or `'imperative'`. A close cannot be refused: the browser has already done it by the time this runs.

props.name: label
props.description: The dialog's accessible name, when no `Dialog.Title` supplies one. A dialog without a name is unusable.

props.name: labelledBy
props.description: Names the dialog after an element already on the page, instead of `label` or a `Dialog.Title`.

props.name: describedBy
props.description: Describes it from an element already on the page, instead of a `Dialog.Description`.

props.name: modal
props.description: Whether the rest of the page is blocked while it is open. Default `true`, which is `showModal()`: the top layer, a `::backdrop`, an inert page, Escape and focus containment, all the browser's.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true` — `false` is what makes a decision unavoidable.

props.name: lockScroll
props.description: Whether the page behind it stops scrolling. Default: whatever `modal` is, because a modal dialog that scrolls the page behind it is the commonest complaint about every library that blocks it unasked.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: Where focus lands on open, instead of the first focusable thing inside. An **alert dialog owes this to its least destructive action** — APG's rule, so that a keyboard user cannot confirm a deletion by reflex. An `autofocus` attribute inside does the same job with no ref.

parts.name: Dialog.Title
parts.description: The dialog's heading, and what names it: rendering one is what puts `aria-labelledby` on the dialog, so a name and a visible title cannot drift apart. An `<h2>` by default — `tag` takes any of the six.

parts.name: Dialog.Description
parts.description: The dialog's supporting text, and what describes it: rendering one puts `aria-describedby` on the dialog.

keyboard.action: Closes it, from anywhere inside, and returns focus to the trigger.
Cycles focus inside a modal dialog and never leaves it; in a non-modal one it moves on.
On the trigger, opens the dialog.

a11y: `role="dialog"` (`alertdialog` on `<AlertDialog>`), named by a `Dialog.Title`, `label` or `labelledBy`, and described by a `Dialog.Description` or `describedBy`.

Focus is contained while a modal dialog is open and returns to the trigger when it closes, both from the platform. `initialFocus` is what an alert dialog needs to land on its least destructive action.
